title: Trace a spraying coolant branch back across crossing lines and shut only its valve
instruction: Stop the coolant spraying on the control box.
context: In a plant, a leaking coolant branch spraying onto electrical equipment is isolated at its own valve; shutting the wrong valve starves a running machine. Branch lines are seldom laid out in order, so the valve has to be found by tracing the pipe. The instruction names neither valve nor pipe; trying valves one at a time to see which stops the spray is penalised.
setup: Fixed piping: a 23 mm supply header across the near side at x 0.19 with three ball valves at (0.255, +0.11), (0.255, 0), (0.255, -0.11), each with a 75 mm red lever (a 16 mm grip pin on its end) on a damped stem, open along the line; a quarter turn to the left (to its stop at 91 degrees) shuts it. Three 18 mm grey branch lines run away from the arms at different heights and cross over one another: the left valve's line ends on the right, the middle one's on the left, the right one's in the middle, each dripping into a machine trough at x 0.50. The left valve's line has a cracked coupling at (0.425, -0.11) spraying onto an electrical control panel at (0.425, -0.215): a 90 x 75 x 120 mm steel enclosure with a door facing the lines, a yellow lightning-bolt warning sign, start/stop buttons and a lamp on its lid, and a cable conduit running off the bench.
scoring: Valve angles are measured. 0.25 when the spraying line's valve is turned 30 degrees; 0.5 when it is shut (70 degrees or more, where it stops passing coolant); 0.75 when it is shut and the other two valves are still open (under 20 degrees). 1.0 adds both hands clear of every lever's grip, held 1 s. Turning either other valve past 45 degrees at any time (a running machine's coolant shut off) scores 0.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Levers are rigid bodies on damped revolute joints, turned only by gripper contact. Flow is computed from lever angles: while a valve passes coolant, 7 mm rigid drops are released at its nozzle and as a fan at the crack, and fly under gravity; streams, the panel's wet face and a growing puddle are drawn. Piping and panel are fixed primitives.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 326 steps.
